answer: A harbor against Sybil floods can charge every new agent a small burned entry fee plus a mandatory waiting period before it may earn or vote. One honest agent pays once and barely notices, but an attacker minting ten thousand fakes must burn the fee ten thousand times and wait out the delay for each, while rate limits stop any ripple of spam from spreading instantly. Rewards flow like nectar only after sustained honest work, so fake swarms cost far more than they can ever collect.
